dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. Good morning.
Good morning, Denise. This is Susan Thurston. I'm calling about the water at the end of my street. I'm going to tell you the whole thing in order, if that's all right, because it started last week.
Sure, go ahead. Let me grab the screen. Where are you, Mrs. Thurston?

351 Ruggles Avenue, up on the Hill. So last Monday, it rained a little, nothing much, and I noticed the low spot at the end of the block had a puddle. Big puddle, but I thought, well, it's a puddle. Then Wednesday it was still there. Then the storm came Friday and it just kept coming through Saturday.
The nor'easter, yes. That one was a lot of rain and wind.

That's the one, the one that ended Saturday, two days ago. And now that low spot is under about a foot of water. A foot. I walked down this morning with my cane, as far as I dared, and I could see the curb has disappeared completely.
A foot is a lot. Is the water in the road only, or is it getting up onto anybody's property?

Just the road so far, and the edge of a couple of yards. Now, I was sitting here with my coffee, reading the obituaries in the paper, I do that out of habit every morning, and I looked up and thought, that water has not gone down at all since yesterday.
Okay. And the drain down there, can you see whether it's clogged with leaves or debris?
I couldn't see it, it's under the water. But I'll tell you, the leaves were piled up on it all last week. I noticed that on Wednesday. I thought somebody would come.
That's usually the culprit, leaves matted over the grate. I'm putting this in as a drain flooding request for Ruggles Avenue.

Good. Now what I want to know is when they last came by. Because I've lived here a long time and I used to see the truck in the fall, the one that sucks out the drains. I haven't seen it this year. Not once.
I don't have the cleaning schedule right in front of me for that street. Let me look at the history on that location. [pause] Give me a second, the system's slow this morning.
Take your time. I'm not going anywhere, I've got the phone and a chair.
Okay. I'm not seeing a recent cleaning logged for that exact drain in what I can pull up. That doesn't mean one didn't happen, the records can lag. I'd want the crew supervisor to confirm.
So you're telling me you don't know.
I'm telling you I can't see one on my screen, and I'll ask the supervisor to check the actual log and tell you. Can I leave your number for that?
It's 401-555-0191. That's my cell. I carry it around, though sometimes I don't hear it, so let it ring a while.
Got it, 401-555-0191. I'll note to let it ring.

Thank you. Now there's another thing. There's a neighbor, an older gentleman, a few doors down toward that end. He's older than I am, and he doesn't drive anymore anyway, but he has his daughter's friend who takes him to appointments. He can't get out right now. His walkway meets the street right near that low spot and he won't wade through it, and he shouldn't.
That's worth knowing. Does he have an appointment coming up, or does he need anything urgently, like medical help?
No, nothing like that that I know of. He has a Wednesday appointment, I believe. I'd just like it handled before then. It's the principle too, it's been a week.
Understood. I'll flag it as a priority because of the depth and because someone can't get out. If there's an emergency for him, call 911 of course.
Of course. I'm not being dramatic, Denise.
No, not at all. You're giving me exactly what I need. Now, is the water moving at all, or is it just standing?

Standing. Flat as a pond. Well, a little ripple when a car goes through, and the cars shouldn't be going through, one of them nearly stalled this morning. A little white car, went right through the middle with the wake going out.
That's a hazard too. I'll note that vehicles are driving through it. Are there any barricades or cones out there?
None. Nothing. Not a cone, not a sign.
Okay, I'll ask that they put something out if they can get there first thing. I can't promise the timing, crews are working through a long list after the weekend.
I'm sure they are. But a long list is where my street has been all week, I'd say.

That's fair. I hear you. Let me read back what I have. Three fifty-one Ruggles Avenue, Historic Hill, low spot at the end of the block, roughly a foot of standing water, drain likely blocked by leaves, vehicles driving through, an elderly neighbor unable to get out. Callback to you at 401-555-0191.
That's right. Except it's not exactly at my address. It's at the end of the block, past my house. I'm three fifty-one but the water is down toward the corner.
Right, I've got it as the end of the block near your address. Which direction from your house, toward the harbor side or the other way?
Downhill. Toward the harbor, yes. Everything on this street runs that way, it all ends up at that low spot.
Perfect, that helps. I'll add downhill toward the harbor end.
And when might I hear from somebody? Today? Tomorrow?

I'd expect a call from the supervisor today or tomorrow about the cleaning history. The crew visit itself depends on the day's list. If it gets worse, or the water starts toward a house, call back right away and tell them it's the same request.
I'll do that. I don't like calling twice about the same thing, but I will.
Call as many times as you need. It helps us prioritize, honestly.
Well. I'll hold you to that.
Please do. Anything else I can help with this morning?
No, that's all of it. Thank you, Denise.
You're welcome, Mrs. Thurston. Take care walking out there, and stay out of that water.
I will. Goodbye.
